State:{'question': 'What is RAG in Gen AI?', 'answer': [{'type': 'text', 'text': '**RAG** stands for **Retrieval-Augmented Generation**. It is a framework in Generative AI that enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) by fetching relevant data from external knowledge sources (such as private databases, documents, or live web feeds) before generating a response.\n\nThink of a standard LLM as taking a **"closed-book exam"**—it relies solely on memory acquired during pre-training. With RAG, the LLM takes an **"open-book exam"**, where it can look up facts from a specified textbook or database to answer the question accurately.\n\n---\n\n### Why is RAG Important? (The Problems It Solves)\n\nStandard LLMs face several key challenges:\n1. **Hallucinations:** LLMs sometimes confidently output false or fabricated information.\n2. **Outdated Knowledge:** LLMs are limited by their training cutoff date.\n3. **Lack of Proprietary Access:** LLMs do not inherently know company-specific or private data (e.g., internal HR policies or customer records).\n\nRAG solves these problems by providing the model with accurate, real-time, domain-specific information right when the query is made.\n\n---\n\n### How RAG Works (Step-by-Step)\n\n1. **User Query:** The user inputs a question (e.g., *"What is our company\'s return policy for damaged electronics?"*).\n2. **Retrieval:** The RAG system searches an external database (often a **Vector Database**) to find relevant text passages or documents.\n3. **Augmentation:** The system combines the user\'s original query with the retrieved documents to construct an enriched prompt:\n   > *"Using the following context: [Retrieved Documents], answer the user\'s question: [Original Query]"*\n4. **Generation:** The LLM reads the augmented prompt and generates a well-structured, accurate response grounded strictly in the provided context.\n\n---\n\n### Key Benefits of RAG\n\n* **Higher Accuracy & Reduced Hallucinations:** Answers are directly grounded in trustworthy, user-provided context.\n* **Cost-Effective Updates:** Instead of spending thousands of dollars fine-tuning or re-training an entire model with new data, you simply update your external vector database.\n* **Source Attribution:** Systems using RAG can cite their sources, giving users clear references for where information came from.\n* **Data Security & Control:** Private enterprise data stays secure in local databases rather than being exposed during model training.', 'extras': {'signature': ''}}], 'attempts': 2, 'quality_ok': True, 'logs': ['Attempt :1', 'Evaluated answer as : False', 'Attempt :2', 'Evaluated answer as : True']}Next:()----------------

State:{'question': 'What is Fine Tuning in Gen AI?', 'answer': [{'type': 'text', 'text': '**Fine-tuning in Generative AI (GenAI)** is the process of taking a pre-trained model (a "foundation model" like GPT, Llama, or Stable Diffusion) and training it further on a smaller, specialized dataset to adapt it for a specific task, domain, or style.\n\n---\n\n### An Analogy: The Medical Student\n* **Pre-training:** Imagine a medical student completing general education and learning how to read, write, and understand general science. (This is like a general AI model learning language and world knowledge from the internet).\n* **Fine-tuning:** That same student spends 3 years specializing exclusively in cardiology. They aren\'t learning language from scratch; they are adapting their existing intelligence to master a specific domain.\n\n---\n\n### Why Fine-Tune a Model?\n\n1. **Domain Specialization:** General models might know basic legal or medical concepts, but fine-tuning allows them to understand complex jargon, industry protocols, or proprietary company data.\n2. **Behavior & Style Alignment:** You can train a model to consistently adopt a specific brand voice, persona, or output format (e.g., always responding in valid JSON or markdown).\n3. **Task Optimization:** Improving accuracy for specific tasks like code generation, translation, sentiment analysis, or summarizing customer support tickets.\n4. **Cost and Efficiency:** Training a massive foundation model from scratch costs millions of dollars. Fine-tuning an existing model requires significantly less data, compute power, and time.\n\n---\n\n### How Fine-Tuning Works\n\n1. **Start with a Pre-trained Model:** Select a base model (e.g., Llama 3, Mistral) that already understands general language or imagery.\n2. **Prepare Specialized Data:** Gather high-quality, labeled datasets tailored to your target task (e.g., 1,000 examples of customer service queries paired with ideal responses).\n3. **Continue Training:** Feed this dataset into the model. The model\'s weights (parameters) are slightly adjusted to favor the new patterns in your data.\n4. **Evaluation:** Test the fine-tuned model to ensure it performs well on the niche task without suffering from **"catastrophic forgetting"** (losing its general capabilities).\n\n---\n\n### Common Types of Fine-Tuning\n\n* **Full Fine-Tuning:** Updates all the weights in the neural network. Highly accurate but computationally expensive.\n* **Instruction Fine-Tuning:** Trains the model using prompt-response pairs to make it better at following specific human directions (how base models become "chat" assistants).\n* **Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT):** Methods like **LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)** or **QLoRA** freeze most of the base model\'s parameters and only train a tiny layer of additional parameters. This drastically lowers GPU memory requirements and cost.\n* **RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback):** Uses human ratings to guide fine-tuning, steering the model to be safer, more helpful, and unbiased.\n\n---\n\n### Fine-Tuning vs. RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)\n\nA common point of confusion is when to use **Fine-Tuning** vs. **RAG**:\n\n| Feature | Fine-Tuning | RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **Best For** | Changing **how** the model behaves, formats, or speaks (Style/Task). | Supplying **what** facts the model knows (Knowledge/Retrieval). |\n| **Data Freshness** | Static (requires re-tuning to update data). | Dynamic (connects live to databases/documents). |\n| **Hallucination** | Reduces formatting errors; can still hallucinate facts. | Reduces factual hallucinations by citing sources. |', 'extras': {'signature': ''}}], 'attempts': 2, 'quality_ok': True, 'logs': ['Attempt :1', 'Evaluated answer as : False', 'Attempt :2', 'Evaluated answer as : True']}Next:()----------------
